newsitem.title: USA: Barnett to acquire Oxford Rescources for $570 million.
newsitem.headline: Barnett to acquire Oxford Rescources for $570 million.

text.p: Barnett Banks Inc. said Tuesday it agreed to acquire auto loan and leasing firm Oxford Resources Corp. in a deal valued at $570 million.

Oxford, based in Melville, N.Y., provides leases and loans for new and used automobiles through more than 2,000 auto dealers in 21 states across the country and had total lease and loan originations in 1996 of about $1 billion. Barnett said Oxford was the nation's largest independent automobile leasing company.

Under the terms of the agreement, Oxford shareholders would receive 0.9085 shares of Barnett common stock for each share of Oxford common stock in a tax-free exchange. Based on the closing price of Barnett shares Monday the deal would be worth $570 million.

"This acquisition is a significant step toward enhancing Barnett's automobile finance business, which is already one of our strengths," said Barnett Chairman Charles Rice. "The number of consumers choosing to lease rather than buy new or used automobiles is increasing dramatically.

Jacksonville, Fla.-based Barnett, which originates about 25 percent of all automobile loans in Florida, said the agreement ensures that Oxford's management will remain in place. It said it expects the transaction to close by mid-year 1997.

Barnett also said its board of directors has authorised the repurchase of up to 15 million shares of Barnett's common stock, in addition to the 20 million shares authorised to be repurchased in 1995. The company has bought back around 15 million shares from the original authorisation.
Barnett's stock was up $1.375 at $42.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
